extracted.intended_audience: general readers, journalists, researchers, and media-watchers seeking background on PolitiFact and fact-checking practices
extracted.subtask_description: An overview of the standards, practices, scope, and criticisms used to evaluate or produce journalistic fact-checking at PolitiFact (including its Truth-O-Meter system, claim selection, sourcing, trackers, corrections, and debates about bias and transparency).

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth-O-Meter rating system
rubrics_metrics.description: Each statement evaluated by PolitiFact receives a 'Truth-O-Meter' rating; the ratings range from 'True' for statements the journalists deem accurate to 'Pants on Fire' for claims the journalists deem 'not accurate and mak[ing] a ridiculous claim'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article references multiple rating labels in practice (e.g., 'Mostly False', 'False', 'Pants on Fire') and notes PolitiFact published a 'step-by-step process of assessing an item's truth' that reveals confirmed facts and includes accreditations. Critics and commentators have urged improvements to the rating system to better address irresponsible, unprovable, or dubious claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of statements (news judgment)
rubrics_metrics.description: PolitiFact's journalists 'select original statements to evaluate' and choose which facts to check 'based on news judgment' — checking 'claims that we believe readers are curious about, claims that would prompt them to wonder, "Is that true?"'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is framed as editorial/news judgment; however, studies and commentators have criticized PolitiFact for lack of transparency about how comments are selected and raised the possibility of selection bias (e.g., analyses finding different rates of false ratings by party). Selection transparency and representativeness are thus evaluation criteria used by observers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of subjects to fact-check
rubrics_metrics.description: The site focuses on the accuracy of statements made by elected officials, candidates, their staffs, lobbyists, interest groups and others involved in U.S. politics; a related site, PunditFact, is devoted to fact-checking claims made by political pundits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PolitiFact also operates specialized trackers (e.g., 'Trump-O-Meter', 'Obameter', Biden Promise Tracker) and local affiliates review promises by regionally relevant elected officials. Scope (political actors vs pundits vs public claims) defines what gets evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of original sources and expert interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporters and researchers 'use original reports rather than news stories' and, 'when possible, PolitiFact uses original sources to verify the claims and interviews impartial experts.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Florida Times-Union noted PolitiFact 'uses strict journalistic standards' in this respect. Reliance on primary documentation and impartial expert interviews is presented as a methodological standard and a basis for credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tracking campaign promises and progress
rubrics_metrics.description: PolitiFact monitors the progress elected officials make on their campaign promises via ongoing trackers (e.g., 'Trump-O-Meter', 'Obameter', 'Biden Promise Tracker') and local variants (e.g., 'Haslam-O-Meter', 'Walk-O-Meter').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These trackers evaluate promise fulfillment over time rather than single utterances, implying longitudinal evidence collection and status updates as part of fact-checking practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction and re-evaluation policy (evidence-updated judgments)
rubrics_metrics.description: PolitiFact has retracted and revised past fact-checks when subsequent information or scientific judgment changed (example: PolitiFact retracted a fact-check about a COVID-19 lab-leak origin and later changed its evaluation to 'unsupported by evidence and in dispute').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organization documents that ratings can change as evidence evolves; this demonstrates a standard of revising judgments in light of new or disputed evidence and of acknowledging uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological limits and uncheckable statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Observers and critics note that some statements cannot be truly 'fact-checked' and that there are only a finite number of statements amenable to thumbs-up/thumbs-down fact-checking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a recognized limitation of the fact-checking approach: not all claims are verifiable in binary terms, and PolitiFact has been criticized for attempting to check statements that may be unprovable or depend on interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and accountability (criticisms and evaluation of bias)
rubrics_metrics.description: PolitiFact has faced allegations of political bias from both left- and right-leaning outlets; academic and media studies have analyzed its distribution of ratings across political parties and questioned transparency about claim selection and treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics use measures such as party-level distribution of 'false' or 'pants on fire' ratings, selection transparency, and responsiveness to critique as yardsticks for evaluating PolitiFact's impartiality and accountability. PolitiFact leadership has responded by citing news judgment and data; external actions (e.g., Meta ending a fact-checking partnership) also factor into credibility assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on original reporting rather than secondary aggregation
rubrics_metrics.description: PolitiFact emphasizes original reporting practices—'using original reports rather than news stories'—as central to verifying claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This editorial standard is highlighted as a distinguishing practice versus simply aggregating other outlets' fact-checks; it supports the organization's claim to produce independent verification based on primary evidence.
